guitar.guitaristsText: Eric Clapton (lead, Leslie bridge part, overdubbed solo); George Harrison, credited as "L'Angelo Misterioso" (rhythm)
guitar.evidence: Two independent lines: the Christie's 2004 auction description of Clapton's 1964 ES-335 states it was used to cut Badge at IBC Studios in December 1968; the Where's Eric! archive states the same guitar was used on Badge and other Goodbye tracks. Wikipedia's Goodbye entry and Harrison's own account in I, Me, Mine independently document the Leslie speaker and Harrison's uncredited rhythm part.
guitar.notes: Removed Gibson SG "The Fool" and Les Paul from the previous entry: no source ties either to this session. Basic track cut 21 November 1968 at Wally Heider (Los Angeles) with Harrison; Clapton's lead was overdubbed in December 1968 at IBC (London). Standard tuning.
guitar.source: Christie's 2004 lot description, 1964 Gibson ES-335TDC (relayed by groundguitar.com); whereseric.com, "Gibson Cherry Red ES-335: Eric Clapton's Cream Guitar"; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye_(Cream_album); beatlesbible.com, 21 November 1968 session entry

tone.target: Studio version, Goodbye (1969): rotary-speaker arpeggio at the bridge plus overdubbed lead
tone.profile: Clean-to-edge-of-breakup humbucker tone swirled through a miked Leslie cabinet, with a fatter sustaining lead overdub
tone.summary: The defining element is documented: Clapton played through a Leslie rotary cabinet normally used with a Hammond organ. There is no evidence of fuzz or heavy distortion on this track. On the GP-180 the chain is therefore a low-gain British amp into a 2x12 cab, with the MOD block standing in for the rotary. Drive comes mostly from the amp; a light boost lifts the solo overdub. Reverb stays low because the Leslie already supplies movement and depth.
gearClues: solo overdubbed separately from basic track
no wah, no fuzz on this track
corrections: Removed the Fuzz block: no source supports fuzz on Badge
Added MOD to stand in for the documented Leslie cabinet
Guitar corrected to Gibson ES-335; SG "The Fool" and Les Paul removed
Cab changed from 4x12 to 2x12, closer to a miked Leslie rotor
Amp choice downgraded to hypothesis: no source names the amp

rig.name: Cream - Badge - Valeton GP-180
rig.recommendedGuitar: Gibson ES-335 or any humbucker semi-hollow; neck or middle position, guitar volume around 8

blocks.gap: Utility block, not part of the historical chain. Keep the threshold low so the arpeggio tails are not cut.

alternatives.reason: If the guitar is noisier at higher gain.

blocks.purpose: Lift the overdubbed solo above the rhythm bed.
blocks.gap: Practical adaptation, not documented. In 1968 the level difference came from a separate overdub pass and a cranked amp. Leave it off for the arpeggio section.

alternatives.reason: Adds sustain to the arpeggio without extra grit.
If the amp alone lacks bite at bedroom volume.

blocks.purpose: Low-gain British platform with mid focus and early breakup.
blocks.gap: Hypothesis. No source names the amplifier used on this track, and part of the signal was coloured by the Leslie's own amplification. UK 45 is chosen for its clean-to-crunch range, not for documented provenance.

alternatives.reason: Cleaner and rounder, closer to a Leslie's own voicing.
American clean platform if the UK 45 sounds too aggressive.

blocks.purpose: Approximate a miked 12-inch rotor rather than a stack.
blocks.gap: No rotary cabinet model exists on the GP-180. A 2x12 is closer to the Leslie's single 12-inch rotor and mid-forward voicing than a 4x12.

alternatives.reason: Rounder top end, less British honk.
For the overdubbed solo if more weight is wanted.
Load a Leslie cabinet IR, see improvements.

blocks.purpose: Trim low end, push mids, roll off the extreme top.
blocks.gap: None. The high cut mimics the Leslie horn's limited top end.

blocks.purpose: Stand in for the Leslie swirl on the arpeggio and the lead.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 has no rotary model. Chorus reproduces the pitch shimmer but not the amplitude pulse or the doppler asymmetry of a real rotor. This is the block that carries the identity of the track, so it stays on.

alternatives.reason: Reproduces the amplitude pulse; blend by ear against Chorus.
Slow sweep, often read as closer to a Leslie than chorus.

blocks.gap: Kept low: the rotary already supplies movement, and more reverb blurs the arpeggio.

alternatives.reason: Slightly smoother tail for the solo.

improvements.summary: The rotary speaker is the one element the GP-180 cannot model. Everything else is close enough with stock blocks.

proposals.recommendedAsset: External rotary/Leslie pedal or plugin placed after the cab block
proposals.reason: The Leslie is the documented signature of the track and no GP-180 module reproduces it.
proposals.whenToUse: If the Chorus block fails to convince on the bridge arpeggio
proposals.expectedGain: Correct doppler swirl, amplitude pulse and slow/fast ramp

proposals.recommendedAsset: Leslie 122/147 cabinet IR (static rotor, close mic) loaded into User IR 1
proposals.reason: Captures the horn and rotor drum voicing that a guitar 2x12 cannot.
proposals.whenToUse: Combined with the rotary effect above
proposals.expectedGain: More authentic midrange and top-end roll-off

proposals.recommendedAsset: Second snapshot with Boost off and Chorus depth raised
proposals.reason: The bridge arpeggio and the overdubbed solo were recorded as separate passes.
proposals.expectedGain: Closer match to both sections of the record
